lessons.title: Your First Grid
lessons.concept: Two Sums That Share a Number

play.targetObjective: Fill two empty boxes so every row and every column adds up.
stepByStep: Read a row from left to right, like a sum.
Read a column from top to bottom.
Put a tile in a box and check both lines it sits in.
play.kidTip: Each box belongs to a row and a column. The number must work for both.
play.audioPrompt: Put the tiles in the empty boxes so every sum is true.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The first grid is about the shape, not the arithmetic: sums within 10, so the new idea — one number belongs to two sums — is the only thing being learned.

lessons.title: Three Empty Boxes

play.targetObjective: Fill three empty boxes so every line adds up.
stepByStep: Find a line with only one empty box.
Work out that box first.
Use what you found to finish the others.
play.kidTip: A line with one gap is the easiest place to start.
play.audioPrompt: Three boxes are empty. Fill them so every sum is true.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Three gaps means some line has two, so the child must choose an order. Starting from a one-gap line is the strategy every later lesson relies on.

lessons.title: Sums up to 15

play.targetObjective: Fill the boxes in grids with sums up to 15.
stepByStep: Find a line with one empty box.
Count on from the bigger number.
Check the other line that box sits in.
play.kidTip: To find a missing part, count on from the part you know to the total.
play.audioPrompt: These sums go up to fifteen. Fill the empty boxes.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Totals now cross ten. A missing addend is a subtraction in disguise; counting on from the known part is the bridge.

lessons.title: Sums up to 20

play.targetObjective: Fill the boxes in grids with sums up to 20.
stepByStep: Start with the line that has one gap.
Find the missing number.
Check its row and its column.
play.kidTip: Make ten first: 8 + 7 is 8 + 2 + 5.
play.audioPrompt: These sums go up to twenty. Fill the empty boxes.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Within 20 is the first-grade fluency target, practised here in a format that asks for a missing part as often as a total.

lessons.title: Four Empty Boxes

play.targetObjective: Fill four empty boxes so every line adds up.
stepByStep: Look for a line with one gap.
After you fill it, look again: a new line may have one gap now.
Keep going until every box is full.
play.kidTip: Each box you fill can open up the next line.
play.audioPrompt: Four boxes are empty. Fill them so every sum is true.

lessons.pedagogyTip: With four gaps, the one-gap line changes as the child works. Noticing that the board has changed is the planning skill.

lessons.title: Take-Away Grid

play.targetObjective: Fill the boxes in a grid where every line takes away.
stepByStep: Read each row: the first number, take away the second.
Read each column the same way, top to bottom.
Put a tile in and check both lines.
play.kidTip: Take away means the answer is smaller than the first number.
play.audioPrompt: Every line takes away. Fill the empty boxes.

lessons.pedagogyTip: All-minus grids are always consistent at the corner, so the child meets subtraction in the grid without mixed signs. Zero can now be an answer.

lessons.title: Plus and Minus

play.targetObjective: Fill the boxes when some lines add and some take away.
stepByStep: Look at the sign in each line before you start.
Add on a plus line, take away on a minus line.
Check both lines for each box.
play.kidTip: Read the sign first. It tells you whether the answer gets bigger or smaller.
play.audioPrompt: Some lines add and some take away. Fill the empty boxes.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Mixed signs force the child to read each line's sign rather than assume one operation for the whole board.

lessons.title: Three Gaps, Two Signs

play.targetObjective: Fill three empty boxes in grids with plus and minus.
stepByStep: Find the line with one gap.
Read its sign.
Fill that box, then look for the next one-gap line.
play.kidTip: If the gap is the first number of a take-away, add the other two.
play.audioPrompt: Three boxes are empty. Some lines add and some take away.

lessons.pedagogyTip: A gap in the first place of a subtraction (? − 3 = 4) needs the inverse operation; this is the lesson where that case starts to appear regularly.

lessons.title: Up to 30

play.targetObjective: Fill the boxes in grids with numbers up to 30.
stepByStep: Start with the line that has one gap.
Use tens and ones to add or take away.
Check the row and the column.
play.kidTip: Split a number into tens and ones: 24 is 20 and 4.
play.audioPrompt: These numbers go up to thirty. Fill the empty boxes.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Numbers up to 30 bring in two-digit addition and subtraction without regrouping pressure.

lessons.title: Four Gaps, Two Signs

play.targetObjective: Fill four empty boxes in grids with plus and minus.
stepByStep: Find a line with one gap and fill it.
Look again for the next one-gap line.
Check every line at the end.
play.kidTip: When you are stuck, try a tile and check both of its lines.
play.audioPrompt: Four boxes are empty. Plan where to start.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The unit's capstone: two signs, four gaps, numbers to 30. A child who finishes this can plan a sequence of inverse operations.

lessons.title: Find the Sign

play.targetObjective: Choose plus or minus so the line is true.
stepByStep: Look at the line with the empty sign box.
Is the answer bigger or smaller than the first number?
Bigger means plus. Smaller means minus.
play.kidTip: If the answer is bigger than the first number, the sign is plus.
play.audioPrompt: Choose plus or minus for the empty box.

lessons.pedagogyTip: All the numbers are shown, so the task is purely about the relation between them. Comparing the result with the first number decides the sign.

lessons.title: Two Signs

play.targetObjective: Choose a sign for two empty boxes.
stepByStep: Take one empty sign at a time.
Compare the answer with the first number.
Check every line at the end.
play.kidTip: Bigger answer: plus. Smaller answer: minus.
play.audioPrompt: Two signs are missing. Choose plus or minus for each.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Two missing signs, each on its own line, practise the same comparison twice per board.

lessons.title: Three Signs

play.targetObjective: Choose a sign for three empty boxes.
stepByStep: Find each line with an empty sign.
Decide plus or minus for each one.
Check every row and column.
play.kidTip: Try plus, check the line, and if it is wrong, change it to minus.
play.audioPrompt: Three signs are missing. Make every line true.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Three missing signs on a board of shared numbers. Try-and-check is a legitimate strategy and the hint says so.

lessons.title: Signs and Numbers

play.targetObjective: Fill a missing number and choose two missing signs.
stepByStep: Find the signs on lines where every number is shown.
Then work out the missing number.
Check every line.
play.kidTip: Do the signs on full lines first. Then the number is easier.
play.audioPrompt: Some boxes need a number and some need a sign. Fill them all.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Mixing both gap types asks the child to choose which kind of reasoning comes first; signs on complete lines are always decidable, so they make a good start.

lessons.title: Signs Mix

play.targetObjective: Fill two numbers and two signs in grids up to 30.
stepByStep: Fix the signs on full lines.
Find a line with one gap left.
Fill it, then the rest.
play.kidTip: A sign tells you which way to go. A number tells you how far.
play.audioPrompt: Fill the missing numbers and signs so every line is true.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The capstone of the plus-and-minus units: both gap types with bigger numbers.

lessons.title: Times 2 and 5

play.targetObjective: Fill the boxes in grids that use times 2 and times 5.
stepByStep: Find the line with the times sign.
Count in twos or fives.
Check the other line the box sits in.
play.kidTip: Times 2 is double. Times 5 counts in fives: 5, 10, 15, 20.
play.audioPrompt: Some lines use times. Fill the empty boxes.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The 2 and 5 tables are the easiest to skip-count, so multiplication enters the grid without a recall burden.

lessons.title: Times up to 5

play.targetObjective: Fill the boxes in grids with the 2, 3, 4 and 5 times tables.
stepByStep: Find a line with one gap.
If it says times, think of the table.
Check the row and the column.
play.kidTip: If you know 4 × 3, you know 3 × 4 too.
play.audioPrompt: These grids use the times tables up to five.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Tables 2–5. Commutativity is worth naming in the tip because the grid shows both orders on crossing lines.

lessons.title: Times up to 10

play.targetObjective: Fill the boxes in grids with every times table up to 10.
stepByStep: Find a line with one gap.
For a missing factor, ask: what times this makes that?
Check both lines.
play.kidTip: A missing factor: 6 × ? = 42. Count in sixes to 42.
play.audioPrompt: These grids use every times table up to ten.

lessons.pedagogyTip: A missing factor is division thinking before division is named; the next unit makes it explicit.

lessons.title: Times and Minus

play.targetObjective: Fill the boxes in grids that mix times and take away.
stepByStep: Read the sign on each line.
Multiply on a times line, take away on a minus line.
Check every line.
play.kidTip: Read the sign first, every time.
play.audioPrompt: Some lines multiply and some take away. Fill the empty boxes.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Mixing × with − (not +) prevents the child from treating every non-× line as addition.

lessons.title: Times Mix

play.targetObjective: Fill four boxes in grids with plus, minus and times.
stepByStep: Find a line with one gap.
Use its sign to find the box.
Look again for the next one-gap line.
play.kidTip: Fill a box, then see which line has only one gap now.
play.audioPrompt: Plus, minus and times. Fill all four boxes.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The unit's capstone: three operations and four gaps.

lessons.title: Share by 2 and 5

play.targetObjective: Fill the boxes in grids that divide by 2 and 5.
stepByStep: Find the line with the divide sign.
Ask: how many twos, or fives, make that number?
Check both lines.
play.kidTip: 20 ÷ 5 asks how many fives make 20.
play.audioPrompt: Some lines divide. Fill the empty boxes.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Division by 2 and 5 always comes out whole here, and links back to the skip counting used for multiplication.

lessons.title: Share up to 10

play.targetObjective: Fill the boxes in grids that divide by numbers up to 10.
stepByStep: Find a line with one gap.
Use a times fact you know: 7 × 6 = 42, so 42 ÷ 7 = 6.
Check both lines.
play.kidTip: Every divide fact is a times fact turned around.
play.audioPrompt: These grids divide by numbers up to ten.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Division as the inverse of multiplication: every hint and tip states the related fact.

lessons.title: Times and Share

play.targetObjective: Fill the boxes in grids that multiply and divide.
stepByStep: Read the sign on each line.
Use one times fact for both directions.
Check every line.
play.audioPrompt: Some lines multiply and some divide. Fill the empty boxes.

lessons.pedagogyTip: A board of only × and ÷ makes the fact family visible across crossing lines.

lessons.title: All Four Signs

play.targetObjective: Fill four boxes in grids that use all four signs.
stepByStep: Find a line with one gap.
Read its sign and use the right fact.
Keep going until every line is true.
play.kidTip: Read the sign, then pick the fact that undoes it.
play.audioPrompt: All four signs are here. Fill the empty boxes.

lessons.pedagogyTip: All four operations on one board; choosing the inverse for each sign is the skill.

lessons.title: Four-Sign Hunt

play.targetObjective: Choose plus, minus, times or divide for three empty boxes.
stepByStep: Compare the answer with the numbers on the line.
Much bigger often means times. Much smaller often means divide.
Try a sign and check the line.
play.kidTip: Ask how the answer got from the first number: a little or a lot?
play.audioPrompt: Three signs are missing. Choose from all four.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Missing signs from all four operations. Estimating size (a little bigger, a lot bigger) narrows the choice before computing.

lessons.title: Big Grid

play.targetObjective: Fill the boxes in a bigger grid where each line has three numbers.
stepByStep: Each row and column now has three numbers before the equals sign.
Find a line with one gap.
Work it out and check the line that crosses it.
play.kidTip: With three numbers, add or take away one step at a time.
play.audioPrompt: This grid is bigger. Each line has three numbers. Fill the empty boxes.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Three operands per line. Every generated line gives the same answer left to right as with the order of operations, so no reading of the line is taught wrongly.

lessons.title: Big Grid With Times

play.targetObjective: Fill five boxes in big grids with plus, minus and times.
stepByStep: Find a line with one gap.
Do times before plus and minus.
Check the crossing line.
play.kidTip: Times comes first in a line: 2 × 3 + 4 is 6 + 4.
play.audioPrompt: A big grid with times. Fill all five boxes.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Times within a three-number line. The generator only builds lines where left-to-right and order of operations agree, so the tip can state the real rule.

lessons.title: Big Grid, All Signs
lessons.concept: All Four in a Long Line

play.targetObjective: Fill five boxes in big grids with all four signs.
stepByStep: Find a line with one gap.
Do times and divide before plus and minus.
Check the crossing line.
play.kidTip: Times and divide first, then plus and minus.
play.audioPrompt: A big grid with all four signs. Fill the empty boxes.

lessons.pedagogyTip: All four operations in three-number lines.

lessons.title: Six Gaps

play.targetObjective: Fill six empty boxes in a big grid.
stepByStep: Find every line with one gap.
Fill those first.
Look again: filling a box can leave another line with one gap.
play.kidTip: Each box you fill can open up the next line.
play.audioPrompt: Six boxes are empty. Plan where to start.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Six gaps on a big board: the planning load rises while the arithmetic stays the same.

lessons.title: Eight Gaps

play.targetObjective: Fill eight empty boxes in a big grid.
stepByStep: Start from a line with one gap.
Keep looking for the next one.
When no line has one gap, try a tile and check it.
play.kidTip: When you are stuck, try a tile in a short line and check it.
play.audioPrompt: Eight boxes are empty. This is the master grid.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The final lesson: eight gaps, all four operations. Sometimes no line has a single gap and the child has to test a tile.
